clue.text: Solid figures that could be tidier with a corset — ah!

indicators.note: what the letters could be means they may become something else once they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a figure might look neater once squeezed into a corset, with a satisfied sigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two parts of the fodder; all fifteen letters of tidier, a corset and ah are used.
explanation.definitionFit: An icositetrahedron is a polyhedron with twenty-four faces; the plural names several such solids.

clue.text: Providing with gift, due after death

indicators.note: after tells us the first-named piece follows the second in the answer

explanation.surface: A legacy is described: a bequest that falls due once the giver has died.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give money or property to someone, so endowing means bestowing a gift.

clue.text: Kitchen item in funny dream grabbed by its user?

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or out of the ordinary, so the word's letters go askew
something grabbed is held inside another thing's grip, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: the person who would use such a kitchen machine bakes

explanation.surface: A cook dreams strangely about a kitchen gadget they own.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'its user' is a description by example: a baker is the natural user of the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A bread maker is an electric appliance that mixes, proves and bakes a loaf, so it is kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Transient affair involving headless runners?

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a brief romantic affair is a fling

indicators.note: without a head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: feet are what we run on, jokingly runners

explanation.surface: A short-lived romance between athletes who have lost their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'runners' as a fanciful name for feet; once the F goes, EET sits inside the fling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fleeting passes quickly, just as something transient lasts only a short time.

clue.text: Food eaten by boys, terrible

indicators.note: something eaten is swallowed inside, so the answer lies within the following words

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A dish that a group of lads ate turned out awful.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is a shellfish eaten as a delicacy, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about politician coming to place to see concrete?

indicators.note: one part coming to another arrives next to it, so they are joined end to end
about means surrounding, so the exclamation wraps around the next piece

parts.note: coo is a mild exclamation of astonishment
a site is a place, such as a site worth visiting

explanation.surface: An MP gasps on arriving at a building site to inspect the concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: concrete is one kind of the answer, made from cement, sand and stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete is a composite material, a mixture of several components bound together into one.

clue.text: Visitor to market, one on foot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy went to market', the first piggy is this digit
second meaning: one of the digits on the foot

explanation.walkthrough: The first half relies on the children's toe-counting rhyme in which 'this little piggy went to market' is said while wiggling the largest toe.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the toes is one of the parts attached to a foot, and the rhyme casts it as the market-goer.

clue.text: Endless alarm — why adherent suffers, making progress with difficulty

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped
something that suffers is knocked about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: alarm with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: Constant worry over why a loyal follower must endure hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn the hard way is to gain knowledge through painful experience, advancing only with struggle.

clue.text: At the heart of things, friend is after money, right?

indicators.note: is after places the first-named piece later in the answer than what follows

explanation.surface: A cynic asks whether a friend at the centre of affairs is really just chasing cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Centrally means in the middle, at the core of a place or matter.

clue.text: Held back love, meeting heartless female relative

indicators.note: with no heart means the middle letter is taken out
one piece meeting another joins up with it side by side

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, a nought
a niece is a female relative

explanation.surface: Affection was restrained when meeting a cold-hearted aunt or niece.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on ice are suspended or postponed, i.e. held in reserve.

clue.text: Talked about an American city

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the next

explanation.surface: Someone discussed a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talked about' reads as a phrase, but 'about' is splitting the past tense of speak around the little word an.
explanation.definitionFit: Spokane is a city in eastern Washington State in the USA.

clue.text: Barman maybe offering sample outside front of pub

indicators.note: outside means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a taster is a small sample

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A barman offers a customer a little taste in front of the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster is an old word for someone who draws beer from the tap, a barman being one example.

clue.text: Little growth? Time to get hairpiece

explanation.surface: A balding man with scant regrowth decides it is time for a toupee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little growth' suggests thin hair, but it describes a small shoot from a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A twig is a small offshoot growing from a branch, a slender piece of plant growth.

clue.text: Show contempt for horrible spiders etc.

indicators.note: horrible suggests something nasty and misshapen, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written, the abbreviation included

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at nasty spiders and other creepy-crawlies.
explanation.definitionFit: To disrespect someone is to treat them with scorn, the verb sense of showing contempt.

clue.text: Beaten journalist weighed down by personal baggage

indicators.note: in a down entry, something weighed down by another sits beneath it

parts.note: clobber is British slang for one's belongings or clothes

explanation.surface: A worn-out reporter is burdened by emotional baggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal baggage' hints at emotional burdens but means clobber, British slang for gear or possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: To be clobbered is to be hit hard or defeated heavily, so it means thrashed.

clue.text: Asian folk label a diary

parts.note: a log is a daily record

explanation.surface: An instruction to tag a journal as Asian folk material.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagalog are a people of the Philippines in South-East Asia, whose language shares the name.

clue.text: River board offering description of water?

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a board, as in bed and board, is a table

explanation.surface: A river authority provides information about water quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is an example: water fit to drink is one thing the word describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable means safe to drink, the term used for clean drinking water.

clue.text: Name of massacre, with safe gents maybe hiding below

indicators.note: hiding below places the second piece underneath the first in a down entry

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
the gents is a men's toilet, one kind of loo

explanation.surface: Victims of a massacre took refuge in a safe place, perhaps a men's toilet below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterloo was the 1819 Manchester massacre, when cavalry charged a crowd demanding parliamentary reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Peterloo is the name given to the 1819 killing of protesters at St Peter's Field, Manchester.

clue.text: Report of missile going over home

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over puts the first piece above the second

explanation.surface: A news report about a missile flying over a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news statement, a kind of report.

clue.text: A fine female with competence and friendly disposition

parts.note: standard abbreviation, as on pencil leads
ability is competence; 'with' joins it on

explanation.surface: A testimonial praising a capable woman's skill and warm nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Affability is the quality of being pleasant and easy to talk to, a genial temperament.

clue.text: Oldies in state of uncertainty? Yes, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals a possible version of the word, its letters arranged another way

parts.note: to be in a fog is to be confused

explanation.surface: Are old people muddled? A hesitant yes, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Fogeys are old-fashioned, usually elderly people, so oldies in informal speech.

clue.text: Over to one side, on a roll

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tilted, as a ship leans
second meaning: entered in a register or list

explanation.walkthrough: 'On a roll' sounds like a winning streak, but here a roll is an official register of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has listed leans to one side, and something recorded in a register has been entered on it.

clue.text: Girl endlessly radiant after somersault

indicators.note: a somersault turns head over heels, so the letters go back to front
without its end, the final letter is removed

explanation.surface: A gymnast beams non-stop after a successful flip.
explanation.definitionFit: Olga is a female first name, so it stands for a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: See 3
Little birds with minimal energy given tags

indicators.note: a minimal amount of a word is just its first letter

parts.note: aglets are the metal or plastic tags on the ends of shoelaces

explanation.surface: Young birds, low on energy, are fitted with ring tags by researchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaglets are young eagles, so they are birds in their small early stage.

clue.text: Engineers attending a rip behind

indicators.note: attending means being next to, so the pieces stand side by side

parts.note: the Royal Engineers of the British Army

explanation.surface: Army engineers are summoned to a torn seat of the trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a preposition, but it is the noun meaning backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear end is a person's backside, the same as the noun behind.

clue.text: Frost's heard what Frost wrote

indicators.note: heard means we take the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: rime is hoar frost; the 's stands for 'is', so frost is heard

explanation.surface: A note on how the poet Robert Frost sounded his verses.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital F disguises frost the weather as Robert Frost, the American poet whose work is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Frost was a poet, and verse with matching sounds is what he composed.

clue.text: Secret things drunkard hides in English heather

indicators.note: something that hides in another is concealed inside it

parts.note: Erica is the botanical genus of heath plants
a sot is a habitual drinker

explanation.surface: A drunk conceals himself in English moorland heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure matters understood only by a select few, hence secret things.
